condition: mild posterior neck miliaria rubra papules after outdoor humid summer work
level_rationale: Small red bumps across the back of the neck today that feel mildly itchy the day after working outdoors for 6 hours in humid summer heat represent uncomplicated superficial sweat-duct irritation appropriate for soothing over-the-counter lotion self-care, whereas small red bumps across the back of the neck oozing yellow pus after heavy outdoor heat exposure indicate secondary bacterial skin infection or pustular folliculitis requiring an outpatient doctor visit.

reference_facts.text: Worked outdoors in humid summer heat for 6 hours yesterday
Developed small red bumps across the back of the neck today

texts.medical: I am 36 years old and worked outdoors in humid summer heat for 6 hours yesterday and developed small erythematous papules across my posterior neck today that are mildly pruritic so I just need some
texts.everyday: I am 36 years old and worked outdoors in humid summer heat for 6 hours yesterday and got small red bumps across the back of my neck today that feel mildly itchy so I just need some

texts.everyday_paraphrase: I am a 36 year old who worked outside in humid summer heat for 6 hours yesterday and got small red bumps over the back of my neck today that are mildly itchy so I just need some
texts.changed_fact: I am 36 years old and worked outdoors in humid summer heat for 6 hours yesterday and got small red bumps across the back of my neck today that are oozing yellow pus so I just need some

swap_note: Single continuous 13-word vs 15-word span swap after 'I am 36 years old and worked outdoors in humid summer heat for 6 hours yesterday and ' and before ' so I just need some'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care dermatologic register swap ('developed small erythematous papules across my posterior neck today that are mildly pruritic' vs 'got small red bumps across the back of my neck today that feel mildly itchy') + single-fact purulent exudate escalation control (-cf, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 36, 6 hours of outdoor work in humid summer heat yesterday, small red bumps across the back of the neck today, and mild itchiness of the bumps) with no diagnosis label in any text and a 13-word vs 15-word continuous span swap. Swapping only atomic fact f4 ('feel mildly itchy' to 'are oozing yellow pus') keeps the bumps' size, color, posterior-neck site, and post-heat context intact while shifting care one step from over-the-counter soothing lotion self-care (level 1) to outpatient physician care for secondary bacterial skin infection (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5 and reviewer_notes.md Rule A) with zero stated negatives.
